question: Will Texas have filed a notice of appeal of Judge Pitman's prison air-conditioning injunction as of October 16, 2026?

calls.reasoning: TDCJ and AG Paxton publicly committed to appealing Pitman's 9/22/2026 permanent injunction, and Texas AG typically files NOAs quickly in high-profile injunction cases (often paired with stay motions). But as of ~2 weeks after judgment no NOA, 5th Cir docket, or stay motion has been reported; the FRAP 4(a)(1)(B) 60-day window runs to ~Nov 21, the most burdensome near-term obligation (progress reports) starts March 2027, and a Rule 59(e) motion (due ~Oct 20) could toll the deadline. NOAs often go unreported, so one may already exist on the docket. CourtListener docket could not be fetched (403/429). No human prediction market found on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi.

- Texas AG press release exists titled 'AG Paxton: Texas Will Appeal Prison Heat Ruling' (texasattorneygeneral.gov); body unreadable (HTTP 402), date unknown; future-tense title.

- Injunction terms: immediately create/implement AC plan; completion by 12/31/2029; progress reports every 6 months starting March 2027; cost ~$1.5B.
- Deadlines: FRAP 4(a)(1)(B) 60 days -> ~2026-11-21. Rule 59(e) motion deadline 28 days -> ~2026-10-20; such a motion would toll the appeal clock (a reason a NOA could come later).
- Stay pending appeal (FRAP 8) normally requires a NOA first; no stay motion reported.
- Texas AG practice in other Pitman cases (e.g., CCIA v. Paxton 2026) involved prompt appeal + stay motions; Paxton is on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot.
- NOAs are short and often not covered by press; absence of reporting is weak evidence of absence.
- Markets: searched Polymarket/Manifold (harness) + web; none found.
- Status quo: no NOA reported. Resolves off public docket (CourtListener/PACER) or credible reporting, not statements of intent.
- Event window: 2026-09-22 -> 2026-10-16 23:59 CT; as of 2026-10-06 ~58% elapsed (14 of 24 days).

calls.reasoning: TDCJ and the AG publicly said they will appeal. I found no reported notice of appeal, Fifth Circuit docket or stay motion through Oct 6, and CourtListener's search API shows the last filing on 9/25. The 60-day government deadline runs to about Nov 21. The first compliance deadline (status report Mar 22, 2027) creates no urgency. A Rule 59(e) motion (due ~Oct 20) could come first and toll the appeal deadline. On the other side, the Paxton AG office often files fast in high-profile cases, the order's 'immediately create a plan' language may push a stay motion with an accompanying notice, and a notice may already be on PACER but not yet in RECAP. Fourteen days of no filing points to no rush, so I put it slightly below even odds. No human market found on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi.

calls.reasoning: Final judgment was entered 9/22/2026. The state has 60 days (FRAP 4(a)(1)(B), to ~11/21) and the first compliance report isn't due until March 2027, so there is no deadline pressure. A timely Rule 59(e) motion (due ~10/20) would also pause the clock. The free CourtListener docket now shows every entry through #359. Entries 352-359 are all transcripts filed 9/28, with no notice of appeal or stay motion, and news through 10/6 reports only the intent to appeal. For filing soon: repeated public promises from TDCJ and AG Paxton, the AG office's habit of filing quickly in high-profile cases, transcript filings that may point to appeal preparation, and Paxton's 11/3 election. With 14 of 24 days gone quietly, a filing in the last 10 days is somewhat less likely than not.
calls.reconciliation: There was one factual dispute: whether a notice of appeal was already on the docket, given that entries 352-355 were not visible to the runs. I re-queried the CourtListener RECAP search API. Entries 352-359 are all 'Transcript Filed' entries dated 9/28, the last entry is #359, and nothing mentions an appeal or a stay. That settles it as far as the free copy goes, though that copy can lag the official docket. Two news searches through 10/6 found only statements of intent to appeal and no filed notice. The remaining disagreement is judgment: how quickly the AG files without deadline pressure. Fourteen quiet days with no stay motion move me a little below the runs. The transcript filings point slightly toward appeal preparation, but that does not offset the silence.
